title: Bounded Autonomy: Between Free Will and Determinism — Angus J. McLean, Oliver
talk_summary: A conceptual talk from an ad-agency AI director arguing that LLMs are closed, non-learning 'flexible databases' whose agentic gains come mostly from context windows, so builders should impose constraints, keep solutions simple, and treat data as multiple representations.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of filling the window, they ask how little context still completes the task, and treat context as a soft constraint to shape rather than a bucket to fill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maybe how little of the context window can you use and still get the task done is a more interesting question

takeaways.what_they_do: He replaced a complex CV-generation pipeline with four letters of HTML and got a large improvement, arguing models default to overcomplicated solutions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it didn't work as well as four simple letters. Those four simple letters were HTML

takeaways.what_they_do: They store the same knowledge in several forms — markdown for human hierarchy, graphs for relationships, clusters for large text, folders for fast retrieval, timelines where relevant — rather than one blob.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ideally you should use multiple representation structures

takeaways.technique: Decompose into small repeatable workflow chunks
takeaways.what_they_do: He cites Adam Smith's pin factory: capitalism breaks tasks into small repeatable chunks, and structured workflows have proven more effective than loose agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: capitalism naturally breaks tasks down into small easily repeatable chunks. And often we have found workflows to be far more effective

takeaways.what_they_do: They deny the model internet access and instead feed high-quality documentation, reporting better results and less susceptibility to SEO/promotional noise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: not giving the model access to the internet and instead giving it high quality documentation, you'll get much better results

takeaways.technique: Don't automate what you can't do manually
takeaways.what_they_do: He argues you should be able to perform a job yourself before automating it, and shows a report built from clustering 50k tweets into strategies as the target output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't automate a job unless you can do it yourself
